claims.claim_ar: فعل أمر موجه للجماعة (صيغة الأمر مع واو الجماعة) من الجذر ذَكَرَ
claims.claim_en: Imperative addressed to a plural addressee ('remember' / 'mention'), formed from the root ذَكَرَ (with plural/waw marker).

claims.claim_ar: «نعمة» اسم يدل على الفضل/النعمة؛ هنا محدَّدة بـ«نعمة الإسلام» أي فضل الهداية والإسلام
claims.claim_en: The noun 'ni'mah' denotes a blessing/favor; in this context it specifically refers to the blessing of Islam (نعمة الإسلام).

claims.claim_ar: اسم الجلالة «اللَّه» (اسم الإله)؛ تقليدياً تربط بالأصل الثلاثي الهـ/ـلـ/ـه
claims.claim_en: The proper name 'Allah' (the God); conventionally linked in traditional morphology to the triliteral root اله.
claims.needs_review_reason: Etymology/derivation of the divine name 'Allah' is treated differently across sources; attribution to root اله is conventional but debated.

claims.claim_ar: مِيثَاق على وزن مِفْعَال (اسم يدل على العقد/الرباط/الميثاق) مشتق من جذر وثق
claims.claim_en: 'mīthāq' is on the pattern mifa'al (مِفْعَال), denoting a covenant/compact derived from the root وثق.
claims.needs_review_reason: Assignment to the exact nominal pattern (مِفْعَال) is standard but some analyses treat related forms differently (derivation vs. denominal formation).

claims.claim_ar: فعل على وزن (فاعَلَ) — صيغة III (مُفاعَلَة/فاعلة) من الجذر وثق، بمعنى عاقدكم/وثقكم به
claims.claim_en: Verb is Form III (فاعَلَ) 'wāthaqa' (واثَقَ), meaning 'he contracted/pledged you by it' — the Form III (reciprocal/associative) flavor of root وثق.

claims.claim_ar: «سمعنا وأطعنا» عبارة بايعية/التزامية تُستخدم للتعبير عن القبول بالسمع والطاعة (صيغة تعهد وولاء)
claims.claim_en: The phrase 'sami'na wa aṭa'nā' functions as a pledge formula: 'we hear and we obey,' expressing acceptance and commitment (often used in pledge/oath contexts).

claims.claim_ar: أَطَعْنَا: فعل ماضٍ متصل بضمير المتكلم الجمع «نا» — من الجذر (طاع/طوع) والاسم المقترن أَطَاعَ
claims.claim_en: Perfect (past) verb with 1st-person plural suffix '-nā' meaning 'we obeyed', from the root طاع (lemma أَطَاعَ).

warnings: Claims were produced only for words/phrases that appear as exact substrings in the provided source chunks. Several words in the ayah (e.g. word_index 6, 8, 9, 10, 13–19) did not have matching source substrings in the chunks and therefore no morphology claims were extracted for them.
Etymological note: the derivation of the divine name 'اللَّه' (claim for word_index 3) is conventionally cited as from root اله but is debated in scholarship; see needs_review_reason for details.
